findings.summary: The machine config is read with hand-written line matching and serde_json instead of a TOML parser.
findings.evidence: write_machine_config writes the value with Rust `{:?}` (Debug) formatting, and wiring.rs:75 reads it back with a TOML parser. The new code instead strips a `claude_bin` prefix and decodes the value as JSON. Debug, TOML and JSON escape some characters differently (for example `\u{..}`), so an unusual path could be read differently here than in wiring.rs. xtask already depends on `toml`. Simpler and more correct: parse the file with `toml`, or share the reader with wiring::claude_bin.

findings.summary: athena.toml is rewritten by line matching and ignores which TOML section a line is in.
findings.evidence: The command rewrites the first line that starts with `claude_version =` in any section. That is safe for today's file: athena.toml:50 is the only `claude_version` line, and the command errors when no line matches. `toml_edit`, already a workspace dependency, could edit `agents.claude_version` exactly while keeping the formatting. Not a blocker.

findings.summary: docs/decision-links.toml is on the deliverables list but was not changed.
findings.evidence: D154 links to no earlier decision, so the criterion's condition never applies and no entry is needed. The list just named the file in case one was.

summary: The change does what the retry asked for. The Claude Code pin is still an exact match. The refusal now names the version it found, the pinned version, and the command `cargo run -p xtask -- repin`. That new command reads `--version` from the same binary Athena runs (`claude_bin` in the machine config, else `claude` on PATH) and rewrites only the quoted value on the `claude_version` line of athena.toml. Running it a second time changes nothing. An empty or non-numeric version, a probe that fails, or a file with no `claude_version` line all stop with an error and leave the file as it was. I ran the targeted tests myself in this snapshot: athena-agent 2 of 2 passed, xtask 2 of 2 passed. The refusal test checks for the new command text, so it would fail against the old message. fmt, clippy and the full test suite come from Athena's recorded CI run for this commit. D154 is a new number, it records the alternatives and the cost, and it links to no earlier decision, so docs/decision-links.toml needs no entry. CHANGELOG and README describe the command. athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh and .github are unchanged, and nothing out of scope was touched. Two minor points: the command reads two TOML files with hand-written line matching, although xtask already has the `toml` crate and the workspace has `toml_edit`.
